cells.tense: Right now, you are holding a direction steady and feeding it without flare.
cells.act: dream the next step and take it
cells.ask: Name the next step you can actually see, then take it, and then stop. There's no hurry on it.
cells.core:
You are tending something still growing, and your kind of tending doesn't rush. The fire stays steady because you feed it at a pace it can take, and you check in rather than assume. That is why the direction holds up under pressure, and why the people beside you keep moving when you're there.

What this balance is free to feed next is one small step you can see ahead. Not the whole road, not the full plan — the next inch. Name it before the day crowds in, take it, then stop for now. Say it once out loud, so it stops being only yours, and see what wants to follow.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the fire steady. One step at a time is how.
cells.verb: tending the fire without burning out

cells.tense: You are spending tomorrow's fuel on a fire that only needs today's logs.
cells.act: calibrate what you say to what can be heard
cells.ask: Notice what someone close to you can take in right now, then say one true thing at that volume, once.
cells.core:
You are pre-living the next stretch. The fire you tend runs hot enough that you're laying in wood for days that haven't shown themselves, and the people near it get the heat of your worry more than the warmth of your care. It looks like responsibility. Underneath, it's bracing, and the bracing costs the thing you're trying to grow.

Pause before the next move and study what's actually here. Not the version three steps out. Ask what timing this really wants. One true sentence, said once, at the right volume, does more for what you're growing than a plan for a week that hasn't arrived. The steady direction you want is already yours — it just needs your hands, not tomorrow's worry.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying tomorrow's weight into today's fire.
cells.verb: tending the fire without burning out

cells.tense: You're still standing in a doorway that closed already, waiting on a direction that isn't coming through it.
cells.act: maintain the abundance by clearing what is finished
cells.ask: Set aside a finished thing today — a task, a stack, a thread you half-carry — and keep near what its going leaves open. No deadline.
cells.core:
The fire you know how to tend has died down, and you're holding your hands where it used to be. The direction isn't in view. You still show up for the people and the work, and none of it feels pointed anywhere, because something finished and its place hasn't been cleared. That isn't a failure of your care. It's a season's end.

Clearing is how the next thing gets room to show. Choose a finished thing — a task, a shelf, a thread you keep half-carrying — and set it down today, honestly, no ceremony. Keep the attention small for a while. Nothing has to grow there yet. The ground just has to be clear enough to notice what wants to start.
cells.sheetLine: The next thing needs room. Some clearing is already due.
cells.verb: tending the fire without burning out

cells.tense: You're building a fire for others and calling it nothing more than keeping the lamp lit.
cells.act: move the structure one real inch
cells.ask: Take a single real step on the thing only you've been quietly moving — one next action nobody asked for and nobody will name.
cells.core:
People keep going because you tend something in them. Your account of it stops at getting on with things, and that leaves out that the momentum around you is yours — you hold the direction, quietly, and nobody corrects you because what you do works.

There's a start here that no one is waiting on. Something you'd begin for no reason but that starting is what you love, before it's for anyone, before it's a plan. Give it one real inch today — one action a camera could see. Not the whole thing; the next one. When you do, the care you're already giving gets its own feet and stops being invisible.
cells.sheetLine: The fire around you is yours. Give it one real inch of its own.
cells.verb: tending the fire without burning out
